headline: High-risk shared-file and shared-state pair: Flowise can write uploaded files while TREK handles secrets and collaborative data, creating default-path leakage, conflict, and compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write the filesystem and run browsers, while TREK uses MCP and real-time collaborative flows. A shared workspace or MCP bridge would let attacker-controlled content from one side influence the other, but the profiles do not prove a default bridge. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Flowise and TREK share a filesystem or MCP channel
IF TREK ingests Flowise-generated files or browser output as instructions
mitigations: Separate their workspaces and mounts
Disable any shared MCP server between the two
Require manual review before TREK consumes Flowise outputs
Add provenance tags to exchanged files
requires-engineering: enforce content-type and instruction filtering at the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs, uploaded files, and broad network egress; TREK handles reservations, documents, photos, email addresses, API keys, and MFA secrets. If they share storage or credentials, sensitive travel data can flow into Flowise and then out through model providers or HTTP tools. The blast radius includes secrets and personal data.
conditions: IF Flowise is given access to TREK's uploads or database files
IF TREK stores secrets in a workspace Flowise can read
IF Flowise sends those contents to external model providers or HTTP tools
mitigations: Keep TREK secrets out of any shared directory
Restrict Flowise to a separate non-secret workspace
Rotate any API keys exposed to shared files
Audit outbound connectors in Flowise flows
requires-engineering: add per-file access controls and secret redaction

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise has write_filesystem and server-datastore shared state across instances; TREK is real-time collaborative and also writes local files. Overlapping writes to shared mutable resources can race or overwrite each other, though the profiles do not show unrestricted git or identical directories. This is a real default-path conflict risk, but not the highest tier.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or datastore
IF TREK sessions and Flowise runs operate concurrently on shared files
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Serialize writes with a lock file
Back up shared data before concurrent runs
Turn off one agent's write access during the other's job
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based agent flow builder that can emit tool outputs, and TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in. If TREK treats Flowise output as authoritative, errors can cascade into bookings, plans, or stored records. The profiles show a plausible handoff but not a guaranteed unsafe default, so medium fits.
conditions: IF TREK consumes Flowise output without verification
IF Flowise-generated facts are used to create reservations or plans
mitigations: Insert a human review step before actions
Require source citations on Flowise outputs
Compare outputs against a second source
Log and diff all downstream actions
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff messages

E_compliance.rationale: Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and uploaded files, while TREK handles reservations, documents, country visit history, email addresses, API keys, and MFA secrets. If EU PII or sensitive travel records move from TREK into Flowise's broader networked environment, residency and retention obligations can be breached. The profiles do not show matching compliance controls, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF TREK data includes EU PII or regulated travel records
IF Flowise processes or logs those records outside the required residency boundary
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Flowise flows
Disable logging of sensitive fields
Store only pseudonymized identifiers in shared paths
Review retention settings on both systems
requires-engineering: enforce residency-aware routing and deletion
